questions.prompt: The Battle of Bunker Hill was actually fought primarily on what nearby hill?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Breed's Hill. They built the fortifications in the wrong place. History kept the wrong name. Sounds about right.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Breed's Hill. Everybody calls it the Battle of Bunker Hill. But that's not where most of the fighting happened.

questions.prompt: The USS Constitution earned what nickname, and in which war?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Old Ironsides. War of 1812. British cannonballs bounced off her sides. Hull was made of live oak. Toughest wood on earth.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Old Ironsides. War of 1812. That ship over there's the oldest commissioned warship still afloat. Show some respect.

questions.prompt: How tall is the Bunker Hill Monument in feet?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: 221 feet. 294 steps. No elevator. Sully used to race me up there. Lost every time but never stopped trying.
questions.npcReactionWrong: 221 feet. You see that obelisk up there? I've climbed it a hundred times. 294 steps, no elevator.

questions.prompt: What famous order did Colonel Prescott give to the colonial troops at Bunker Hill?
choices: Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes
Save your powder for the officers
Hold the line at all costs
Fire at will when they reach the trenches
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes. Ammunition was scarce. Every shot had to count.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes. Every kid learns that in school. You shoulda known.

questions.prompt: The Charlestown Navy Yard built warships for the U.S. Navy for how many years before closing?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: 1800 to 1974. 174 years. My grandfather worked here. My father worked here. Then they said we weren't needed anymore.
questions.npcReactionWrong: 174 years. 1800 to 1974. This yard built ships for almost two centuries. Then the government closed us down.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What type of ship is the USS Constitution classified as?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: A frigate. Wooden-hulled, three-masted heavy frigate. Old Ironsides isn't a battleship.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: A frigate. Not a battleship or a destroyer. Know your ships.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What 2010 film about a bank robbery was set and filmed in Charlestown?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: The Town. Hollywood came to Charlestown once. Made a movie about bank robbers. They got some things right.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: The Town. Ben Affleck. Bank robbers. Hollywood nonsense, mostly. But they filmed it here.

alternateQuestions.prompt: The Bunker Hill Monument was funded primarily by what method?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Private donations. Sarah Josepha Hale helped—same woman who created Thanksgiving. Building that monument almost went broke twice.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Private fundraising. They begged for money for years. The government didn't pay for it. The people did.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What bridge connects Charlestown to Boston's North End?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Charlestown Bridge. When you leave here and head back into Boston, that's the one you cross.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Charlestown Bridge. Also called the North Washington Street Bridge. Gets you to the North End.

alternateQuestions.prompt: Who commanded the British forces at the Battle of Bunker Hill?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: General William Howe. The British won the battle but paid a heavy price. Howe led them up that hill three times.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: William Howe. The British won but lost a thousand men. Pyrrhic victory, they call it.

redemptionChallenge.instructions: Put these Revolutionary War events in the correct chronological order.
redemptionChallenge.npcPassResponse: You got it right. Most people mess up Revere's Ride and Bunker Hill. They happened the same year, different months.
redemptionChallenge.npcFailResponse: You put the Declaration before Bunker Hill. The whole point of the battle was we hadn't declared anything yet. Read a book.
